executive_assessment.text: Named 2025 examples differentiate Nord-Est rain damage, southern service/road impacts and conflict-displacement locations.
UNFPA explicitly reports insecurity postponing services for hurricane-affected women and girls, while mobile delivery and remote referrals supplied partial coping capacity.
The August 2026 update supplies dated protection context for Kenscoff and Artibonite, without attributing these displacements to climate.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-02-24 reports: UNICEF reports May 2025 heavy rains inundated about 3,900 homes in Nord-Est; Melissa later damaged schools, latrines and water systems especially in southern departments.

Source dated 2026-02-24 reports: Following Melissa, UNICEF reports cholera outbreaks in Bainet, Marigot, Belle-Anse, Grand-Gosier and Thiotte, exposing vulnerabilities where climate shocks damaged services.

Source dated 2026-02-24 reports: UNICEF reports violence-driven site growth after Mirebalais/Saut d’Eau attacks and displacement in Petite-Rivière; most displaced people lived outside formal sites or with hosts.

Source dated 2025-11 reports: UNFPA reports November 2025 insecurity postponed planned distributions and mobile clinics, including support for hurricane-affected women/girls around Petit-Goâve and southern areas.

Source dated 2025-11 reports: Melissa damaged Grand’Anse roads and isolated communal sections; Les Cayes hospital flooding and minor Jérémie/Port-de-Paix damage were reported separately from insecurity restrictions.

Source dated 2025-11 reports: UNFPA reports mobile clinics reached 2,453 Melissa-affected people in Petit-Goâve, alongside separate internally displaced populations in metropolitan and Artibonite sites.

Source dated 2025-10 reports: The October 2025 assessment reports gang passage fees and restricted agricultural-input delivery along RN1/RN2/RN3, while Melissa separately flooded displacement sites in metropolitan Port-au-Prince.
Source dated 2025-10 reports: Melissa road damage disrupted Jacmel–Port-au-Prince connections and Belle-Anse/Marigot supply and emergency-access routes.

Source dated 2025-10 reports: FEWS NET reports funding-related inability to preposition cyclone-season food, compounded by violence-related access interruptions and logistics costs near displacement sites.

Source dated 2026-09 reports: UNFPA’s August 2026 snapshot reports violence displacement in Kenscoff, Dessalines and Petite-Rivière and constrained access to prompt care for sexual-violence survivors.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 27 of 27 evidence records and 6 of 6 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The bank lacks a current, high-resolution and internally consistent numeric baseline and scenario set for cyclone, flood, heat, drought, rainfall, and sea-level hazards across Haiti.

Independent evaluation is limited to the WFP portfolio through 2022; municipal DRM, adaptation, humanitarian, social-protection, and climate-security outcomes and unintended effects remain largely unevaluated.

The fcv-to-climate reverse pathway is supported through displacement, access, and service disruption, but quantitative estimates of conflict's additional effect on climate losses, adaptation, and recovery are absent.
Distributional evidence for disability, age, gender, livelihood, host-community status, and different urban and rural settings is incomplete and not consistently linked to hazard exposure.
Melissa impact counts vary across agencies and reporting dates; source-specific snapshots are not pooled or treated as present caseloads.
UNFPA and UNICEF service outputs do not establish independent protection effectiveness, avoided losses or climate-change attribution.
PAHO December 2025 original PDF returned 403 and was not used. FEWS NET’s expired forecasts were excluded; only historical observed-context passages retained.
The August 2026 protection update has no climate mechanism; it is contextual FCV evidence, not a climate-attributed caseload.
The 2025 insecurity-related service postponements are documented during hurricane response, not just inferred from overlapping maps; no October 2026 route safety is implied.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
